# Original column matches truth

`original_column_matches.tsv` holds fifteen independently authored complete reports for raw YAML and captured CSV. Every field and six successful exact CSV artifacts were enumerated and compared with actual reference Python execution before the candidate was exercised. Candidate observations never write expected truth. Only backend and runtime/engine versions are normalized.

Search is unanchored unless the authored pattern supplies anchors. Missing values pass. Unicode scalar matching, lookahead and backreferences retain the portable contract. Wrong column kinds and invalid syntax are deferred until the owning converted column checkpoint, even for empty input; earlier conversion failures take precedence. A held record survives a later conversion failure. A compound case pins an earlier invalid pattern before a later pattern that exceeds compilation policy: the earlier REQ-0827 remains deferred at its owning checkpoint. Later declaration vocabulary is still scanned before study capture, while unreachable payload compilation stops. Invalid pattern findings contain only the original pattern at the pattern path and keep earlier completed records.

An additional reference assessment found that empty patterns fail schema minimum length before source capture; it is outside this checkpoint fixture. The unchanged negative-sex-code and negative-matches-bad-pattern documents have separately authored full reports. Existing committed expected CSV and error files are unchanged.

Both installed hosts replay all fifteen cases twice with cached source capture, exact complete observations, success publication bytes and failed-save gates. R stays inside the Python-free PATH guard.
